segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: Thanks for joining. Today I'd like to understand how bookings work now, and what you need from the new app.

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Sure. Right now patients phone the front desk, and we lose a lot of calls during busy hours.

segments.speaker: FRONTDESK
segments.text: Mondays are the worst. The phone rings non -stop between 8 and 10.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: So the main goal is online booking. Who should be able to book?

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Patients should be able to book an appointment online without creating an account. Just a name, a phone number and an email.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: Should they pick a specific physio, or just a time?

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: They should be able to choose a practitioner and see that practitioner's available times.

segments.speaker: FRONTDESK
segments.text: And we need to block out times ourselves, for staff meetings and leave.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: What about reminders?

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Patients should get an SMS reminder the day before their appointment.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: Do you want to take payments online?

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Um, I think, maybe a deposit. I'm not sure our patients would like paying up front. We'd have to see.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: Okay, I'll note that as an open question. What about cancellations?

segments.speaker: FRONTDESK
segments.text: People should be able to cancel online, but not less than 24 hours before the appointment.

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Yes, and if they cancel later than that, they should call us.

segments.speaker: DEVLEAD
segments.text: From our side, is there an existing system we need to connect to?

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: We use clinic desk for patient records. The bookings should show up there automatically.

segments.speaker: DEVLEAD
segments.text: Do you know if Clinic Desk has an API?

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Ah. I believe so. Probably. I'd have to ask them.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: How fast does the booking need to be?

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: It just needs to be fast and easy to use, especially on phones.

segments.speaker: DEVLEAD
segments.text: Are there any rules about where the data is stored?

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Patient information has to stay in Australia. That's non -negotiable.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: Great, I'll write this up, and we'll review it next week.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: Last week we covered booking, reminders and cancellations. Has anything changed since then?

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Yes, we talked about guest booking, but now I think patients should log in, so they can see their history.

segments.speaker: FRONTDESK
segments.text: Um? Honestly, I'm not sure about that. A lot of our older patients won't want another password.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: Could we allow both? Log in if you want, or book as a guest.

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Yes, that works. Guests can still book, and patients with an account can see their past appointments.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: On payments, did you decide about the deposit?

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Yes, we'll take a $20 deposit, for new patients only.

segments.speaker: DEVLEAD
segments.text: Will the deposit be refunded if they cancel?

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Only if they cancel more than 24 hours before.

segments.speaker: FRONTDESK
segments.text: About reminders. Many patients have told us they prefer email.

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Then send both. An email two days before, and the SMS the day before.

segments.speaker: DEVLEAD
segments.text: I checked clinic desk. They do have an API, but it's read only for appointments.

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Oh, um, so, the front desk would have to enter them twice. That's... not great.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: We'll look at options and bring them to the next meeting.

segments.speaker: FRONTDESK
segments.text: One more thing, we need a waitlist, so if someone cancels, the next person gets offered the slot.

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Maybe. Let's... Let's not promise that for the first version.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: I'll mark the waitlist as a candidate for a later release.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: Today we'll confirm the open items. First, clinic desk.

segments.speaker: DEVLEAD
segments.text: Clinic Desk can import a daily CSV file. We can export new bookings to it every night.

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Nightly is fine. Same day bookings can be checked in the app.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: Next, the waitlist.

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: We'll leave the waitlist out of the first release.

segments.speaker: FRONTDESK
segments.text: That's fine, as long as it's on the list for later.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: On performance, last time we said fast. Can we put a number on it?

segments.speaker: DEVLEAD
segments.text: How about this? The available times load in under two seconds on a phone connection.

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Two seconds sounds right.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: And for accessibility?

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Um, I guess it should work with screen readers. I don't really know what the standard is.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: I'd suggest WCAG 2 .2 level AA, I'll send you a short summary.

segments.speaker: OWNER
segments.text: Okay, let's go with that.

segments.speaker: ANALYST
segments.text: Great. I'll update the requirements document and share it by Friday.
